A bored pile hole doesn't stay open by luck.
On soft or filled ground, the bore wall wants to slump before the concrete ever goes in.

The fix isn't more mud. It's weight and seal, holding the wall open on pressure while you drill deeper.

That same fluid has to build a thin skin on the wall fast, a filter cake, before it leaks into the ground and you lose that pressure.

Get the density and the seal right and the hole waits for the pour. Get it wrong and you're re-drilling a collapsed pile.
What's the trickiest ground you've had to hold open on a pile job?

Construct Gel is built for piling ground, not HDD ground.
Bored piles and diaphragm walls go deep into soft, saturated ground, and the bore has to hold until the pour.

Construct Gel builds the density to hold the wall open and lays a filter cake fast enough to stop fluid loss.

Dose from 14 to 100 kg per cubic metre depending on ground, most piling jobs run 30 to 45 in conditioned water.

Condition with Soda Ash first, hard water kills bentonite before it starts. Add Filter Low to tighten the seal further on soft or high-loss ground.
Got a piling spec calling for a particular program? Give the team a call and we'll match it.
